objective: Preserve current OCCT unpublished-tail behavior; safe rollback is a temporary partial adapter, not an accepted replacement for native semantics.

current_evidence.observed_gap: Unpublished tail, copy/fill constructor ownership, and growth relocation-constructor failure now have bounded receipts. Remaining old-range destructor exceptions in growth and shrink/Clear can create native dead registered slots; these remain actionable separately. Historical receipts describe their archived implementations.

next_slice.name: Preserve initialized spare slots on native tail-constructor failure
next_slice.storage_model: Keep Vec<T>'s registered initialized prefix [0,len). Its spare capacity may also contain live but unregistered T values, as OCCT does after constructor failure. Do not create dead slots below len or change generic Drop/variance.
implementation: After successful capacity preparation, iterate the requested spare prefix through Vec::spare_capacity_mut. Before each constructor, replace its MaybeUninit slot with MaybeUninit::uninit without Drop: a retry must forget any old unpublished object before attempting native-style placement construction. Write the returned T only when construction succeeds.
Publish the requested length with one reviewed set_len only after every tail constructor succeeds. Do not install LengthRollback or an implicit destructor guard for completed spare values.
If construction panics, retain old len and the successfully initialized spare values. Their omitted Drop is intentional native behavior, and memory-safe resource leakage is permitted by Rust.

A later native-style placement write over a previously initialized spare slot must omit its old destructor. MaybeUninit::write can express that overwrite without creating a reference to a dead registered T.

Freeing or replacing storage must drop only the registered prefix and free the allocation; it must not discover and silently destroy the unpublished tail. Clearing retained storage similarly must not sweep unregistered slots.

Route the explicit native Resize and SetValue extension policies through this core once proven. Keep any rollback convenience variant explicitly named/documented; do not continue counting rollback as native failure parity.
safety_review: Spare slots must be in the currently owned allocation and outside registered len; capacity and overflow validation precede construction.

MaybeUninit<T> permits initialized and uninitialized spare storage. Forgetting a valid T or freeing its backing bytes without running Drop leaks resources but does not itself violate Rust memory safety.

All registered prefix values stay valid on unwind. Rust references into the vector cannot alias the exclusive mutable operation; callback-time C++ alias observers remain a separate explicit adapter problem.
Returning T from a callback still does not promise native address-dependent in-place construction. Keep that remaining callable domain distinct.
Constructor entry points need their own allocation ownership treatment on failure; do not assume successful reuse of this tail core closes copy/fill constructor leak behavior.

acceptance_tests: The existing late-default and late-fill Rust observations must match the original native rows directly, including retained resource counts and absence of tail Drop events. Do not match the recovered rows as native behavior.

Cover first, intermediate and final requested tail-constructor failures, both retained and grown storage, default and fill policies, then retry, overwrite, Clear(false), Clear(true), Reserve and destruction.
Use nonallocating elements with borrowed destructor counters to prove overwrite/free omit unpublished Drop under strict Miri without intentional allocator leaks.

On a failed retry over previously initialized spare storage, track attempted slots separately from completed slots: native placement construction ends the prior object lifetime even if the new constructor throws. Do not repair or drop that failed slot as though its old T were still live; recover leaked payloads through the test-only ownership registry if necessary.

For owning payload cases, record exact constructed spare slots and explicitly destroy them only in test teardown before ordinary allocation cleanup. Label this typed repair as test-only and keep it out of production behavior.

Separate tests that inspect native state before repair from tests validating the repair itself. Assert original-slot destruction and exactly-once cleanup of known live values; never read or drop unwritten spare slots.
Preserve all 49 original LinearVector declarations, compiler body bindings, borrowed lifetime/auto-trait checks, strict provenance and leak checking. No ignore-leaks or permissive-provenance flags.

subsequent_slices.name: Growth old-range destruction exception ownership
subsequent_slices.gap: Replacement relocation-constructor failure now retains native allocation and completed values. After successful relocation, an old-range destructor exception can leave dead registered source slots and a completed untransferred replacement. Rust Vec assignment cleanup differs from that native state.
subsequent_slices.design: Extend the separately reviewed raw lifetime/destructor policy to grow destruction and storage transfer, tracking dead old slots plus completed replacement ownership without creating safe references to invalid values. Native callback-throw prefixes must precede any explicit test-only repair. Do not mark the whole grow method complete from relocation-constructor coverage.

subsequent_slices.name: Destructive shrink exceptions
subsequent_slices.gap: Native destructor exceptions can leave dead registered slots and untouched later values. This is different from unpublished live tail storage.
subsequent_slices.design: Use a separately reviewed unsafe lifetime policy with ManuallyDrop and precise hole/progress recovery obligations if exact malformed native state must be exposed. Keep ordinary safe shrink sound; do not conflate this requirement with the memory-safe unpublished-tail slice.

completion_rule: Close each gap only with direct native-state comparisons and exact method/compiler bindings. Explicit test repair and safe cleanup alternatives receive no native-parity credit.

completed_constructor_slices.name: Copy constructor and insufficient-capacity assignment temporary
completed_constructor_slices.capacity: Exactly source.Size, including retained-empty source producing an unallocated result.

completed_constructor_slices.name: Fill constructor failure ownership
completed_constructor_slices.capacity: Zero for empty fill, otherwise max(2,count), preserving initial Resize growth. Shared unpublished construction transfers ownership only after success; failure retains the allocation and completed copies without implicit destruction or free.

completed_constructor_slices.name: Growth relocation-constructor allocation ownership
completed_constructor_slices.capacity: Native nextCapacity of the existing receiver; old registered storage publishes no replacement until relocation returns. Failed copies/moves retain raw allocation and completed replacement prefix; move source mutations persist. Old-range destructor exceptions remain pending.
